title: Normalized row-cycle comparison with the concrete first-page quotient
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian, def-sp-abelian], $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive left-exact functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and $I$ a commuting bicomplex [def-sp-double-complex-total] with complex index $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution index $r\in\mathbf N$. Assume $I^s=0$ for $s<b$ for some integer $b$. Put $R_s=F(I^s)$ and $J=\operatorname{flip}(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(F)(I))$, extending the resolution index by zero [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and $K=\operatorname{Tot}(J)$. Let $L$ be a decreasing subcomplex filtration [def-sp-filtration] with $L.\mathrm{complexStep}(p,n)=(J.\mathrm{secondFiltration}(n)).\mathrm{step}(p)$ for all integers $p,n$. Let $a_{r,s}:R_s^r\to K^{s+r}$ be the inverse of the extension isomorphism followed by the diagonal coprojection for $(r,s)$. Write $Z_{r,s}=L.\mathrm{complexCycles}(s,s+r,1)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] and $Q_{r,s}=\operatorname{coker}(L.\mathrm{complexBoundaries}(s,s+r,1)\hookrightarrow Z_{r,s})$ with quotient projection $\pi_{r,s}$ [lem-sp-filtered-complex-page-differential]. There are families $e_{r,s}:Q_{r,s}\cong H^r(R_s)$, $t_{r,s}:\mathrm{cycles}^r(R_s)\to (L^sK)^{s+r}$ and $x_{r,s}:\mathrm{cycles}^r(R_s)\to Z_{r,s}$, for every natural $r$ and integer $s$, such that $t_{r,s}$ followed by the filtration inclusion equals $i_{\mathrm{cycles}}a_{r,s}$, $x_{r,s}$ followed by the cycle-subobject inclusion equals $t_{r,s}$ followed by the graded quotient projection, and $x_{r,s}\pi_{r,s}e_{r,s}=\mathrm{homology}\pi_{R_s,r}$. Here row cycles mean the kernel of $R_s^r\to R_s^{r+1}$ with its kernel inclusion; row homology is the cokernel of the incoming boundary map into those cycles, and $\mathrm{homology}\pi$ is that cokernel projection. No page differential is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Write R_s = F(I.X s), J = flip(mappedFunctor F(I)), and n=s+r. The map a_{r,s}: R_s^r -> Tot(J)^n is the inverse extension isomorphism followed by the (r,s) diagonal coprojection. Since r is nonnegative, s belongs to [s,n]. Its image is contained in the second-filtration supremum, hence hL gives a unique lift through the mono (L.step s).arrow.f n. The projection of the diagonal coproduct onto J^(r,s) kills all summands in L^(s+1). Restrict it to L^s, descend to the cokernel, and check the inverse identities on each diagonal summand. This identifies gr^s L in degree s+r with R_s^r. This argument uses [s,n], and does not assume s>=0.

The total differential on a diagonal inclusion is the resolution differential plus the signed complex-index differential. The latter lands in L^(s+1), so only the resolution differential survives on gr^s L. The normalized graded comparison therefore identifies its kernel with row cycles and its image with row boundaries. Apply filteredComplex_firstPage_cycles_boundaries to identify these with L.complexCycles and L.complexBoundaries. Restrict the lifted inclusion to row cycles to obtain t, and factor its graded projection through the cycle mono to obtain x. The inclusion and graded-projection equations are exactly the two claimed normalizations.

The row and filtered cycle comparisons carry the boundary inclusions into each other, so their cokernel universal properties give mutually inverse quotient maps. Compose with the natural extension-by-zero homology comparison at degree r to obtain e. The induced cokernel map sends the cycle class of a row cycle to its row homology class, giving x followed by page projection followed by e.hom = homologyπ. At r=0 the incoming negative-resolution term is zero, so both incoming boundary images vanish. At zero rows all maps are unique zero-object maps. The equations determine t and x by monicity, and e by the epic projection from row cycles; no arbitrary homology isomorphism is chosen.

theorem secondFiltration_row_cycle_comparison
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (I : HomologicalComplex₂ A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ))
    (hbelow : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ s : ℤ, s < b → IsZero (I.X s))
    (L : DecreasingFiltration
      ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).total
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hL : ∀ p n : ℤ, L.complexStep p n =
      ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).secondFiltration n).step
        p) :
    let K := (((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor F).obj I).flip).total
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let R := fun s : ℤ ↦ (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (I.X s)
    ∃ (e : ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : ℤ), filteredComplexPageObject K L 1 (s, (r : ℤ)) ≅
        (R s).homology r)
      (t : ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : ℤ), (R s).cycles r ⟶
        (L.step s : CochainComplex B ℤ).X (s + (r : ℤ)))
      (x : ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : ℤ), (R s).cycles r ⟶
        (L.complexCycles s (s + (r : ℤ)) 1 : B)),
      (∀ r s, t r s ≫ (L.step s).arrow.f (s + (r : ℤ)) =
        (R s).iCycles r ≫ secondFiltrationRowι F I r s) ∧
      (∀ r s, x r s ≫ (L.complexCycles s (s + (r : ℤ)) 1).arrow =
        t r s ≫ (L.complexQuotientπ s (s + 1) (by omega)).f (s + (r : ℤ))) ∧
      (∀ r s, x r s ≫ filteredComplexPageπ K L 1 (s, (r : ℤ)) ≫ (e r s).hom =
        (R s).homologyπ r)
